card: This PR refactors ExternalSignerScriptPubKeyMan to receive the external signer command and chain name from CWallet rather than reading gArgs and Params() directly. It solves an architectural coupling problem where wallet signing paths reached directly into process-wide global state. The change aligns external signer option handling with other wallet settings loaded from WalletContext and adds unit tests to verify parameter injection. No dependencies are declared.
changed_since_previous: Includes a separate test commit adding unit tests for argument propagation and an assertion on debug logs in wallet_signer.py.
evidence: Commit 96bf425361 notes that capturing these settings in LoadWalletArgs matches how other wallet options are loaded from the injected WalletContext and decouples the SPKM from globals.
problem: ExternalSignerScriptPubKeyMan::GetExternalSigner accessed process-wide globals (gArgs and Params()) deep inside descriptor setup and PSBT signing paths. This coupled external signer management to global state instead of the injected wallet context and caused -signer configuration to be re-evaluated on each invocation rather than at wallet load time.

risk.why: A mistake in passing the external signer command or chain string could cause external hardware signers to fail enumeration or address display.

summary: This PR removes direct access to global state from ExternalSignerScriptPubKeyMan by passing configuration parameters down from CWallet. The wallet loads the external signer command and chain string during CWallet::LoadWalletArgs using the injected ArgsManager, caches them on the CWallet instance, and supplies them to the external signer factory methods and GetExternalSigner. Unit and functional test coverage are added to verify argument propagation.
